items.title: 狂賣美債救日元？日本外國證券單月驟減878億美元
items.title_en: Selling U.S. Bonds to Rescue the Yen? Japan's Foreign Securities Drop by $87.8 B in One Month
paras: 日本過去一個月為籌措創紀錄的匯市干預資金，可能出售部分外國證券，包括美國公債。
日本財務省周一(7日)公布的外匯存底資料顯示，截至8月底，日本持有的外國證券較前一個月減少878億美元，降幅接近近期為支撐日元所投入的干預規模。
財務省先前證實，截至8月26日止的一個月內，日本當局投入相當於964億美元的資金干預匯市，創單月歷史新高，其中部分行動與美國聯手進行。
這份資料並未詳細揭露所持證券的種類或到期年限，不過市場人士估計，日本約有70%的外匯存底投資於美國公債。
截至8月底，10年期美國公債價格僅略低於7月底水準，顯示評價變動對外國證券持有額下降的影響極為有限。
日元近期漲勢強勁，短短數個交易日內升值約3%，市場焦點鎖定日本央行（BOJ）升息預期升溫，以及日本政府退休金投資基金（GPIF）可能增加國內資產配置，兩大政策因素正成為推動日元走強的主要動能。
美國銀行最新政策研判認為，日元這波漲勢仍可能延續。
隨著日本央行政策立場轉向偏鷹，此前持續壓抑日元的部分因素正在逐步消退。美銀預期，日本央行可能維持每季升息的步調，目前市場已反映政策利率至2027年7月升至2%的預期。
若日本央行9月升息並釋放鷹派訊號，做空日元的交易邏輯可能進一步弱化。
政策方面，美銀認為，日本政府扭轉日元弱勢的意願正在升高。財務省此前沒有採取激進干預，可能是希望先為日本央行加快升息創造條件。
若升息路徑更加明確、日元卻仍持續走弱，財務省可能透過買進日元進行干預。因此，即使美元受到支撐，美元兌日元的升值空間仍可能受到政策因素限制。
美銀預估，美元兌日元年底將回落至149，並將155視為重要技術關卡。若匯價跌破155，日元買盤可能進一步加速。
高盛也表示，過去幾年日元持續疲弱，很大程度受到美國經濟韌性及日美利差擴大影響；如今日本央行政策方向轉變，加上GPIF可能調整國內資產配置，使日元過去面臨的結構性逆風逐漸減弱，甚至可能轉化為支撐日元的力量。
其中，GPIF可能引發的資金流動尤其受到關注。高盛援引2020年的經驗指出，GPIF當年雖於3月底正式宣布調整外債配置目標，但相關資金流動早在1、2月便已出現，顯示實際資產調整可能早於政策正式公布。
因此，高盛特別關注9月7日公布的8月國際證券交易（ITS）數據，認為其中可能浮現GPIF資金輪動的早期跡象。
另一方面，摩根大通認為，市場對日本央行升息的預期已經偏高。9月升息幾乎完全反映在市場價格中，1年期1年期交換利率升至約2.13%，隱含的緊縮速度甚至高於摩根大通自身預測。
若市場對升息的預期開始降溫，日元反而可能承受壓力。
paras_en: Japan may sell part of its foreign securities, including U.S. Treasury bonds, to raise record‑high foreign‑exchange intervention funds gathered over the past month.

Data on Japan's foreign‑exchange reserves released by the Finance Ministry on Monday (the 7th) show that as of the end of August, Japan's holdings of foreign securities fell by $87.8 billion from the previous month, a decline close to the scale of recent yen‑supporting interventions.

The ministry previously confirmed that over the month ending August 26, Japanese authorities intervened in the FX market with roughly $96.4 billion, a historic monthly high, part of which was coordinated with the United States.
The data do not detail the types or maturities of the securities held, but market participants estimate that about 70 % of Japan's foreign‑exchange reserves are invested in U.S. Treasuries.

By the end of August, the price of the 10‑year U.S. Treasury was only slightly below its level at the end of July, indicating that valuation changes had a minimal impact on the drop in foreign‑security holdings.

The yen has rallied sharply in recent days, appreciating about 3 % over a few trading sessions, with market focus on rising expectations of Bank of Japan (BOJ) rate hikes and the possibility that the Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) will increase domestic asset allocation – two policy factors driving the yen’s strength.
Bank of America’s latest policy view sees the yen’s recent rally as likely to continue.

As the BOJ shifts to a more hawkish stance, some of the factors that have kept the yen suppressed are fading. Bank of America expects the BOJ may keep raising rates each quarter, and markets already price the policy rate up to 2 % by July 2027.
If the BOJ raises rates in September and signals hawkishness, the short‑selling case against the yen could weaken further.

Policy‑wise, Bank of America believes the Japanese government’s willingness to reverse yen weakness is growing. The Finance Ministry’s earlier restraint from aggressive intervention may be aimed at giving the BOJ room to accelerate hikes.

If the rate‑hike path becomes clearer while the yen keeps weakening, the Finance Ministry could intervene by buying yen. Thus, even if the dollar is supported, the dollar‑yen upside may be capped by policy factors.
Bank of America projects the dollar‑yen pair to fall back to 149 by year‑end and sees 155 as a key technical level. A break below 155 could accelerate yen buying.

Goldman Sachs also notes that the yen’s recent weakness over the past few years has been largely due to U.S. economic resilience and widening Japan‑U.S. yield differentials; the BOJ’s policy shift and a possible GPIF reallocation to domestic assets are eroding that structural headwind and could even become a support for the yen.

The potential GPIF‑driven fund flows are especially watched. Goldman cites 2020 experience, when the GPIF announced a change to its foreign‑bond allocation at the end of March, but fund movements began in January‑February, suggesting asset adjustments can precede formal policy announcements.
Accordingly, Goldman is paying close attention to the International Securities Transactions (ITS) data for August released on September 7, seeing it as a possible early signal of GPIF fund rotation.

Conversely, JPMorgan argues that market expectations of BOJ rate hikes are already too high. The September hike is almost fully priced, with the one‑year forward rate up to about 2.13 %, implying a tightening pace even faster than JPMorgan’s own forecast.
If market expectations for rate hikes cool, the yen could instead come under pressure.

paras: 上週稍早，美元兌日元匯率一度攀升至160.39，創7月底美日聯合干預以來的最高水準，但上週四(3日)日元突大幅走強，單日漲幅接近2%，創聯合干預以來最大單日升幅。美元兌日元自160.39高點快速回落，最低下探155.3附近，離7月干預後的低點155.23僅一步之遙。日元上周累計升值約2.5%，創7月底來最大單周升幅紀錄。
不同於7月底，此輪日元急升目前並無明確證據顯示東京當局再次入市干預，日本央行(BOJ)相關數據也未顯示波動由官方直接推動，市場更傾向歸因於BOJ升息預期升溫、日元空頭回補，以及聯準會(Fed)升息預期降溫。
日元此輪急升的直接驅動力，來自日美貨幣政策預期的逆向變動。知情人士透露，BOJ傾向本月將基準利率上調25個基點以應對通膨上行風險。
BOJ審議委員高田創上周表示，升息1碼「並非一定板上釘釘」，一般而言連續升息也有可能，總裁植田和男則明言若判斷金融條件過於寬鬆，完全可能加快升息步伐。
隔夜指數掉期數據顯示，市場對BOJ本月升息1碼定價已接近100%，並完全反映明年1月前再次升息，野村證券更指出，在日元持續疲軟的極端情境下，BOJ可能在12月前的3次會議上連續升息。
美國方面，聯準會理事沃勒上週四表示，美國通膨已出現一些降溫跡象，下一次利率決策將「很大程度上」受即將公布的8月通膨數據影響。偏鴿派表態推動市場削減對9月升息的押注，機率已降至約50%。
目前美國政策利率仍處3.5%-3.75%區間，即使BOJ本月升息至1.25%，兩國利差仍有225至250個基點。
不過市場交易的是方向變化，日本緊縮、美國寬鬆的預期逆轉，正動搖套利交易的基礎。
隨著日元逼近155關口，空頭踩踏風險急劇升溫。摩根大通策略師田中俊雅等人警告，若美元兌日元貶破155，龐大的空頭部位恐被逼加速解除，引發連鎖賣盤。
根據摩根大通估計，目前仍有約16-17兆日元的看空部位尚未平倉，若完全解除，理論上可能將匯價推入142至146區間，但其基準判斷仍是美元兌日元處於155至165區間。
另一重大不確定性來自日本官方。最高外匯事務官員三村淳表示，對近期日元走勢「既不滿意，也沒有感到安心」，日本仍處「高度警戒狀態」，被解讀為可能繼續干預的訊號。分析人士認為，9月18日BOJ會議後恰逢「白銀周」假期，流動性下降，不排除當局利用此時段行動。
paras_en: Earlier last week the USD/JPY rate surged to 160.39, the highest level since the joint US‑Japan intervention at the end of July, but on Thursday (the 3rd) the yen rallied sharply, gaining almost 2% in a single day – the biggest one‑day rise since the intervention. The dollar fell back quickly from the 160.39 peak, sliding to around 155.3, just a hair away from the post‑July low of 155.23. The yen appreciated about 2.5% over the week, the largest weekly gain since the end of July.

Unlike the end‑July move, there is no clear evidence that Tokyo authorities have intervened again, and BOJ data do not show the swing being driven directly by officials. The market attributes the rally mainly to hotter expectations of BOJ rate hikes, short‑covering of yen bears, and a cooling of Fed‑hike expectations.

The immediate driver of the yen’s sharp rise is the opposite shift in US‑Japan monetary‑policy expectations. Insiders say the BOJ is inclined to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points this month to counter upside inflation risks.

BOJ policy‑board member So Takada said a one‑tick hike “is not set in stone” and that consecutive hikes remain possible, while Governor Kazuo Ueda stated that if financial conditions are judged too loose, the bank could accelerate the pace of tightening.

Overnight index‑swap data show the market is pricing a one‑tick BOJ hike this month at almost 100% and fully factoring in another hike before January 2025. Nomura Securities adds that in an extreme scenario of continued yen weakness, the BOJ could deliver three consecutive hikes across its meetings before December.

In the United States, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that inflation is showing some cooling signs and that the next rate decision will be “largely” influenced by the upcoming August inflation data. His dovish tone has pushed the market’s probability of a September hike down to roughly 50%.
The U.S. policy rate remains in the 3.5%‑3.75% band, so even if the BOJ lifts its rate to 1.25% this month, the bilateral spread would still sit at about 225‑250 basis points.
However, what the market is trading is the change in direction – the reversal of expectations toward tighter Japan and looser U.S. policy is unsettling the foundation of carry‑trade arbitrage.

As the yen nears the 155 threshold, the risk of a short‑covering squeeze rises sharply. JPMorgan strategists such as Toshimasa Tanaka warn that if USD/JPY falls below 155, massive short positions could be forced to unwind quickly, sparking a cascade of sell orders.

JPMorgan estimates that roughly ¥16‑17 trillion of short yen positions remain open; if they were all liquidated, the rate could theoretically be pushed into the ¥142‑¥146 range, although the firm still views USD/JPY as residing in the ¥155‑¥165 band.

Another major uncertainty comes from Japanese officials. Senior FX official Jun Mimura said he is “neither satisfied nor reassured” by the recent yen moves and that Japan remains in a “high‑alert” state, a comment read as a possible signal of further intervention. Analysts note that the BOJ meeting on September 18 falls during the “Silver Week” holiday, when liquidity thins, and they do not rule out action during that window.
